about.text: Sweets made from khoa, milk boiled down in an open pan to a stiff dough: cooked with sugar into peda and burfi, or kneaded with flour, fried and soaked in syrup as gulab jamun.

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Which khoa goes into a sweet depends on how dry the sweet must be; the khoa is then worked with sugar and shaped (or, for gulab jamun, kneaded, fried and soaked in syrup).
